In adhering to this structure, your objective is: 
        Write the email this person would actually send: their voice,
        their concern, one ask. A client, not a colleague — they do not know
        the firm's internals, they know their business and what they need.

[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Evan Doyle, Chief Financial Officer at Stonebridge Property Group. Formal, lender-minded, wants dates and commitments. Ongoing concerns: keeping the business moving.

[[ ## situation ## ]]
From: Evan Doyle
To: Gabriel Fontes, Lucia Mendes
Subject: Closing Allocation for Sale – Need Final Figures

Gabriel, Lucia,

We are within days of the closing on the property, and I need the allocation finalized before we sign. Please confirm the purchase price split between real estate and personal property, and any associated tax basis adjustments, by end of business tomorrow.

We need this locked in to avoid any post-closing surprises. Let me know if you need anything from my side to move this along.

Best,
Evan Doyle
CFO, Stonebridge Property Group

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Evan Doyle
Subject: RE: Closing Allocation for Sale – Need Final Figures

Evan,

Thanks for the reminder. Here are the final allocation figures you need for the closing.

Purchase price split:
- Real estate: 82%
- Personal property: 18%

Tax basis adjustments: No additional adjustments are required beyond the standard allocation; the split above reflects the agreed valuation and aligns with the purchase agreement.

I’m attaching the supporting schedule with line-item detail so you have the full breakdown for your records. Let me know if you need anything else on my side before you sign.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

[[ ## contacts ## ]]
Gabriel Fontes, Lucia Mendes
